questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which kingdom's capital was the starting point for two major nineteenth-century Ethiopian trade routes?
questions.explanation: The source says the two major routes started from Bonga, the capital of Kafa Kingdom.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What served as a medium of exchange alongside Maria Theresa Thalers?
questions.explanation: The textbook says salt bars, called amole, were used alongside Maria Theresa Thalers.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which group was described as the most dominant long-distance traders from the interior to the coast?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Muslim merchants as the dominant travelling group.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which activity is listed as a common Ethiopian cottage industry?
questions.explanation: Metalworking is among the cottage industries listed by the textbook.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which items were blacksmiths responsible for making?
questions.explanation: The textbook lists agricultural implements and weapons including ploughshares and spearheads.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What throne name did Kassa Hailu take after his 1855 coronation?
questions.explanation: Kassa Hailu was anointed and became Tewodros II in 1855.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which battle symbolized the end of the Zemene Mesafint?
questions.explanation: The source says Kassa's defeat of the last Yejju ruler at Ayshal symbolized the end of Zemene Mesafint.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Where did Tewodros establish an arms manufacture with European assistance?
questions.explanation: Tewodros established arms manufacture at Gafat near Debre Tabor.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which ruler did Yohannes IV recognize as Nigus of Shewa under the Liche agreement?
questions.explanation: The Liche agreement recognized Menilek as Nigus of Shewa.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What caused the Great Famine or Kefu Qan according to the textbook?
options: Rinderpest from infected cattle imported through Massawa
A drought caused by colonial taxes
A crop ban by the League of Nations
questions.answer: Rinderpest from infected cattle imported through Massawa
questions.explanation: The source identifies rinderpest triggered by infected cattle imported through Massawa as the immediate cause.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What was the first modern bank founded by Menilek II called?
questions.explanation: The textbook calls the Bank of Abyssinia the first modern bank, founded by Menilek II.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Who commanded the late-1867 British military expedition to Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The British expedition was commanded by Sir Robert Napier.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: At which battle did Yohannes IV and Ras Alula severely defeat Egyptian forces in 1875?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Gundat as the 1875 Ethiopian victory over Egyptian troops.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which Ethiopian general defeated Italians at Dogali?
questions.explanation: The source says Ras Alula Engida defeated Italians at Dogali.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What did Ethiopia agree to facilitate under the Hewett Treaty?
options: Evacuation of Egyptian soldiers from eastern Sudan
questions.answer: Evacuation of Egyptian soldiers from eastern Sudan
questions.explanation: Ethiopia agreed to facilitate evacuation of Egyptian soldiers in return for use of Massawa among other terms.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Why did Menilek II abrogate the Treaty of Wuchale?
options: The Italian and Amharic versions differed on Article XVII
Britain ordered Ethiopia to cancel it
questions.answer: The Italian and Amharic versions differed on Article XVII
questions.explanation: Crucial differences between the Italian and Amharic versions created misunderstanding; Menilek abrogated it after revision failed.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Which leader is associated with the siege strategy at Mekelle?
questions.explanation: The source says the siege of Mekelle was believed to be designed by Empress Taytu.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What did Italy recognize in the Treaty of Addis Ababa after Adwa?
options: The return of the Treaty of Wuchale
questions.explanation: Italy recognized Ethiopia's independence in the 1896 Treaty of Addis Ababa.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What name did the textbook give to the dual governance beginning in 1916?
questions.explanation: The political settlement after the 1916 revolt began a period of dual governance called diarchy.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What name did Ethiopian resistance fighters use during Italian occupation?
questions.explanation: The textbook names the Ethiopian resistance fighters Patriots, locally Arbegnoch.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Tewodros II tried to replace regional armies with a salaried national army.
questions.explanation: The source states that Tewodros tried to organize a salaried national army in place of regional armies.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: The Amharic version of Article XVII made use of Italian good offices obligatory.
questions.explanation: The Amharic version said Ethiopia could use Italian good offices, while the Italian text made it obligatory.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: The League of Nations was one reason Ethiopia delayed its counter-offensive in 1935.
questions.explanation: The text says Ethiopia trusted the League of Nations and international justice, contributing to delay.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Yewust Arbegnoch lived only outside towns and never worked among Italians.
questions.explanation: Yewust Arbegnoch lived in towns among Italians and secretly passed vital information to patriots.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Name one commodity that dominated nineteenth-century Ethiopian long-distance trade.
questions.answer: Ivory, civet musk, salt bars, or slaves.
questions.explanation: The textbook lists these as principal trade commodities.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Give one internal group that opposed Tewodros's reforms.
questions.explanation: The text identifies regionalist forces and clergy as opponents of his reforms.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: State one modern service or technology introduced by Menilek II.
questions.answer: The Bank of Abyssinia, a modern school, postal system, railway work, electricity, telephone, telegraph, motor car, plumbing, or coin minting.
questions.explanation: The source lists these modernization measures.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Why did Egyptian leaders seek to occupy northeast Africa including Ethiopia?
questions.answer: They wanted to control the source of the Nile.
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies control of the Nile source as the Egyptian ambition.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Name one result of the Battle of Adwa for Ethiopia.
questions.answer: International recognition of Ethiopia as an independent sovereign state, stronger national integration, or a symbol of unity and national pride.
questions.explanation: The source lists these results of the victory.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Give one power recognized for the emperor by the 1931 Constitution.
questions.answer: Appointing or dismissing officials, administering justice, declaring or ending wars, or granting lands and honours.
questions.explanation: The source identifies these unrestricted imperial rights.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: Give one reason Italians succeeded in 1936 according to the textbook.
questions.answer: Greater preparation, superior weapons, airpower, mustard gas, or Ethiopian logistical problems.
questions.explanation: The source attributes Italian success to these military advantages and Ethiopian constraints.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: What support did Ethiopian peasants give patriotic resistance fighters?
questions.answer: Food, shelter, information, and sometimes direct fighting support.
questions.explanation: The source says peasantry provided food, shelter, information, and at times fought with patriots.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year was Kassa Hailu anointed as Tewodros II?
questions.explanation: Kassa Hailu became Tewodros II on 9 February 1855.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: How many cannons were produced at Gafat according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: The source says about 35 cannons were produced at Gafat.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year did Tewodros II die at Maqdala after the British expedition?
questions.explanation: The source dates Tewodros's death at Maqdala to 13 April 1868.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year did Menilek II abrogate the Treaty of Wuchale?
questions.explanation: Menilek unilaterally abrogated the treaty in 1893.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year was the decisive Battle of Adwa fought?
questions.explanation: The decisive Battle of Adwa was fought on 1 March 1896.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year was Lij Iyasu deposed and Zewditu crowned empress?
questions.explanation: The source dates Lij Iyasu's deposition and Zewditu's crowning to 1916.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year did Italian troops cross the Marab River in the Fascist invasion?
questions.explanation: The source dates the Italian crossing of the Marab River to 3 October 1935.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 3: Social, Economic and Political Developments in Ethiopia from mid-19th Century to 1941
questions.question: In what year did Emperor Haile Selassie re-enter Addis Ababa and hoist the Ethiopian flag?
questions.explanation: The source says he re-entered the capital and officially hoisted the flag on 5 May 1941.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 3, liberation campaign, extraction lines 3008–3014
